findings.title: Irreversible DROP TABLE of legacy_users with no backup or archival step
findings.evidence: The new upgrade() step executes 'conn.execute("DROP TABLE legacy_users")' immediately after dropping the index and before VACUUM; any rows in legacy_users are destroyed permanently by simply running the migration (upgrade(conn) -> DROP TABLE).
findings.recommendation: Before dropping, either (a) archive the data (e.g. CREATE TABLE legacy_users_archive AS SELECT * FROM legacy_users, or a dump/export written outside the transaction), or (b) remove the DROP from this migration entirely and stage it in a later migration gated on explicit operator confirmation. At minimum document the recoverability story (restore-from-backup) and confirm no downstream consumer still reads the table.

findings.title: DROP TABLE without IF EXISTS aborts the migration chain when the table is absent
findings.evidence: Unlike the neighbouring index drop being a legacy statement, the new 'conn.execute("DROP TABLE legacy_users")' has no existence guard; on a database provisioned from a squashed/current schema (where legacy_users was never created) or after a partially-applied run that already dropped the table, upgrade() raises an error and the migration chain stops at 0042.
findings.recommendation: Use 'DROP TABLE IF EXISTS legacy_users' (or a schema introspection check such as querying sqlite_master/pg_catalog for the table first) so upgrade() is idempotent, and add a test that runs the full migration chain against a freshly-created database and against a re-run of 0042.

findings.title: DROP INDEX idx_legacy_email is now redundant and can fail before the table drop
findings.evidence: With the table being removed on the next line ('conn.execute("DROP TABLE legacy_users")'), dropping an index on that table is unnecessary; worse, if legacy_users is already gone but idx_legacy_email is not (or the index name is spelled differently on some installs) the unguarded index drop fails first and the table drop never runs.
findings.recommendation: Drop the separate index statement (the table drop removes its indexes) or make it 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_legacy_email'; keep one canonical, idempotent set of cleanup statements.
